correctness.rationale: In the stated homogeneous tree presentation, finite labelled hulls give exactly the complete ordered tuple types: their incidence structures over the named parameters agree exactly when the map on the marked leaves is a finite partial isomorphism, which extends by homogeneity. The finite extension property supplies realization. Deleting the last leaf either suppresses its trivalent neighbor, identifying the subdivided edge, or lowers its quadrivalent neighbor to a trivalent vertex, identifying the attachment site. With m leaves and Q quadrivalent vertices there are 2m-Q-3 edges and m-2-2Q trivalent vertices. Evaluating these counts in the two predecessor states gives the claimed recurrence, including infeasible states; summing yields the differential form. In arity one the value 3n-3q-5 distinguishes q at fixed n. At n=6 the internal skeletons are a path or star on four trivalent vertices, a path on three internal vertices with the quadrivalent one at its center or end, and an edge between two quadrivalent vertices. At three through five leaves each q determines the skeleton. An independent skeleton enumeration and arity-three series calculation reproduced every entry of the displayed table, without using the frozen verifier.
residual_risks: The series check is finite corroboration; the inverse-deletion proof controls all arities. Only injective new leaves over a pointwise-named base are considered.
